verdicts.rule_check: README.md:369-375 quotes are verbatim. The code does what the README's placement rule says ('later than the stretch's own first row (the owner's message or the stop it starts at)'). That rule itself puts an act stamped between a completed stop and the owner's next message in no stretch. Two statements imply late acts are caught: 'A helper's act is charged to the stretch in which it happens', and the stated cost ('the owner's next turn ("thanks") can be blocked once for a background helper's late commit'). The idle-window case is not among the listed limits (README:377-379).
verdicts.reason: Reproduced independently. Take an ungoverned turn whose background helper commits while the session is idle, with the owner's next message arriving before the helper's completion wake. No stop ever judges that commit. The documents say late helper acts are charged to the next turn. decisions.md:37-40 asks for fail-closed on outward actions where the rule is silent. This gap is neither closed nor stated. Severity is medium because the Stop gate cannot prevent the commit in any case (it only demands governor loads afterwards) and the timing window is narrow.

Whether a current transcript row for such a denial carries toolDenialKind is not established; the README says the flag was observed on 2026-11-16 for a hook denial only. The consequence is one block that loading the governors answers, in a turn that did attempt an outward action.

new_leads: DS-4's repro command as written ('mut.py MU05 MU04') raises KeyError, because mut.py looks up MUTS by full id. The finder's reported output must come from a run with full ids.

All 189 'recorded denials' that DS-3 counts are stream-json output rows (tool_result_meta / non_execution_kind), not session-transcript rows. Nobody has shown whether a transcript row for a headless or prompt denial carries toolDenialKind in the current harness version. That fact decides whether DS-3 happens in normal use.

governance-enforce.py wrote() (the False path of PROMPT_CLASS_SILENT_WITHOUT_OWNER_MESSAGE) ignores the denial flag entirely, while Model.outward uses was_denied. The two tests of whether a call counts as done do not agree.
DS-1's unbounded loop probably applies to the receipt gate too, since receiptlaw.decide uses the same feedback() count. The finder's 'empty all' run reported 4 receipt blocks; I did not re-run it.
With HELPER_ACT_PLACED_BY_TIME = False, MU09 (a helper started AFTER the act also makes it count) survives the table. No case pins the '<= at' window of the False path.
